clue.text: The French FBI agent is one doing the donkey work

parts.note: le is the French masculine form of 'the'
a G-man is American slang for an FBI agent (Government man)

explanation.surface: A French FBI officer is the one stuck with all the drudgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A legman is a subordinate who runs errands and gathers information, doing the tedious legwork for someone else.

clue.text: Hero of romantic comedy does so miss working outside

definitions.meaning: the leading man of a romcom typically ends up winning over the heroine, which is read here as landing the girl
a young woman doing farm work in the open air, as in Britain's wartime Women's Land Army

explanation.surface: A romcom hero behaves just like that, and so does a woman toiling in the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so' joins the two halves. The first half is cryptic: what a romcom hero does at the end is land (the) girl. A Land Girl was a woman drafted into farm work in Britain during the World Wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the British Women's Land Army were young women sent to labour on farms, out in the fields.

clue.text: Get M Roux endlessly cooking for him?

definitions.text: Get M Roux endlessly cooking for him?

indicators.note: cooking stirs ingredients together, so the letters given are mixed into a new order
endlessly takes the final letter off the chef's surname

explanation.surface: Getting Monsieur Roux to keep on cooking would suit a food lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Michel and Albert Roux are famous French chefs working in Britain. 'endlessly' trims ROUX to ROU, and with GET and M those letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmet is a connoisseur of fine food, exactly the diner a top chef like Roux cooks for.

clue.text: Bad breath or containing a bit of niff is noisome

indicators.note: containing says the jumbled letters hold another letter within them
bad breath reads as the word breath gone wrong, so its letters with those of or are jumbled
a bit of takes just the opening letter of niff

explanation.surface: Halitosis, or anything with a whiff of stink, is offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' looks like it describes the breath, but it signals the anagram, giving ABHORRET; 'containing' then puts the first letter of 'niff' inside. Niff is British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or disgusting, and abhorrent likewise describes something repugnant.

clue.text: Blade runner mixed up in Ikea sect

indicators.note: mixed up means confused, so the letters of the two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A runner on a blade is caught up in a cult at the furniture store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blade Runner' looks like the film; it is a runner on a blade, a skate gliding on ice.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice skate runs on a metal blade over ice, so it is literally a blade runner.

clue.text: Old comedy film, a right corny production acting foppishly outside

indicators.note: a production of the words puts them on in a new arrangement

parts.note: camping means behaving in an affected, exaggerated way, and also staying outdoors in a tent

explanation.surface: An old film comedy: a corny staging full of hammy, effeminate acting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' rearranges A, R and CORNY into CARRYON. Carry On Camping (1969) is one of Britain's long-running series of bawdy Carry On comedy films.
explanation.definitionFit: Carry On Camping is a 1969 British comedy film from the Carry On series, now a period piece.

clue.text: Nice items I'm arranging on monument longer than anyone knows

indicators.note: arranging puts the letters of the three words into a fresh order

parts.note: I'm loses its apostrophe and supplies its letters as written
a memorial is a monument raised to commemorate someone

explanation.surface: Tasteful pieces placed around an ancient monument that has stood forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranging' rearranges NICE and ITEMS into SINCETIME; 'on' is just a link in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a span of time reaching back beyond anyone's memory or records.

clue.text: Cut a part of the nose

parts.note: the bridge is the bony upper ridge of the nose

explanation.surface: A slice off a section of the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it, cutting parts out.

clue.text: Urge old flame excited about start of relationship

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for excited goes round the letter

parts.note: hot can mean excited or aroused

indicators.note: start of takes the first letter of relationship

explanation.surface: An excited former lover pushes for a fresh romance.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhort is to urge someone strongly to do something.

clue.text: See 6
A hunger it dealt with having more sauce

indicators.note: dealt with suggests the letters are handled and reorganised, like a hand of cards

explanation.surface: Hunger satisfied by a meal with plenty of sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sauce' looks culinary, matching 'hunger'; here it means cheek or impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce is informal for cheek, so someone with more sauce is cheekier, more badly behaved.

clue.text: Cardinal was prime minister once

definitions.meaning: a cardinal point of the compass, one of four
Lord Frederick ... was British prime minister from 1770 to 1782

explanation.definitionFit: North is a cardinal compass point, and Lord North led the British government during the American Revolution.

clue.text: Stick on gallows, up there is a difficult situation

definitions.text: up there is a difficult situation

parts.note: to gum is to stick with glue
tree is an old word for the gallows

explanation.surface: Glue on the gallows: hanging there would be a real predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link in this across clue. The definition uses the idiom 'up a gum tree', meaning in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'up a gum tree' means stuck in a predicament, so being up that tree is a difficult situation.

clue.text: One giving up playing reedily

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who quits after performing in a thin, reedy way.
explanation.definitionFit: A yielder is one who yields, that is, gives way or surrenders.

clue.text: Finish work losing right to make another attachment

indicators.note: losing says a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: to retire is to stop working for good

explanation.surface: Retiring and giving up rights so as to form a new connection.
explanation.definitionFit: To retie is to tie again, fastening something a second time.

clue.text: Stir men playing lute primarily? He might

definitions.text: Stir men playing lute primarily? He might

indicators.note: playing means the letters of the two words are performed in a new order
primarily picks just the leading letter of lute

explanation.surface: Moving men by playing chiefly on a lute: a medieval singer could do that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges STIR MEN into MINSTRE, and 'primarily' adds L from 'lute'.
explanation.definitionFit: A minstrel was a medieval musician who sang and often played the lute, stirring his listeners.

clue.text: Perhaps watch to see how long performance takes

definitions.meaning: a wristwatch is one example of a clock

definitions.text: to see how long performance takes
definitions.meaning: read as two words, to time a piece is to measure the length of a performance

explanation.definitionFit: A timepiece is any instrument for keeping time, of which a watch is one kind.

clue.text: Nears end painfully caught in trap

indicators.note: painfully suggests the words are twisted, so their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An animal nearing a painful end after being snared.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensnared means caught in a snare, a kind of trap.

clue.text: Song about one Australian that is strongly disliked

indicators.note: about means around, so the song wraps round the letter

parts.note: an anthem is a song of praise or loyalty
A, the indefinite article, can stand for one

explanation.surface: A song about an Australian that people loathe.
explanation.definitionFit: Anathema is something or someone intensely loathed, a thing detested.

clue.text: Faldo and S. African golfer change in America

parts.note: Nick Faldo is the English golfer
Ernie Els is a South African golfer

explanation.surface: Two famous golfers switching over in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' looks like a verb; it means coins, and nickels are US five-cent pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickels are American five-cent coins, the small change in a pocket.

clue.text: 'Mother and Child' one worked in stone

parts.note: ma is informal for mother
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A sculpture titled Mother and Child, carved in stone by an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason is a craftsman who builds or carves with stone.

clue.text: Sign exclusive story mostly about amount of inflation

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened word goes round the measure
mostly drops the final letter of the word

parts.note: a scoop is a news story published first and exclusively
RPI, the Retail Prices Index, is a British measure of inflation

explanation.surface: A sign that an exclusive news story is mainly about inflation figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inflation' suggests economics on the surface, and so it does here: the Retail Prices Index is Britain's long-standing measure of price rises. 'mostly' and 'about' trim the scoop and wrap it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Charm a cross teacher to begin with

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a donkey and a horse

indicators.note: to begin with takes the first letter of teacher

explanation.surface: A good-luck charm for a bad-tempered teacher, at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry' describing the teacher; it is a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm worn to ward off harm or bring luck.

clue.text: Construction set holy place's working back

parts.note: Mecca is the holiest city of Islam

indicators.note: back says the word for working is read in reverse

parts.note: on means working, as of a machine switched on

explanation.surface: A building set at a sacred site is functioning again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses ON to NO. Meccano is a British construction toy of metal strips and nuts and bolts.
explanation.definitionFit: Meccano is a model construction kit of metal strips, bolts and wheels.

clue.text: One leading pack from Lakeland

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the place name

explanation.surface: A leader of a group of hikers or animals from the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: Akela is the leader of a Cub Scout pack, named after the wolf in The Jungle Book.
explanation.definitionFit: Akela is the title of the adult leader of a pack of Cub Scouts.

clue.text: Old man against keeping recipe for light snack

parts.note: pop is informal for father, one's old man

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the word for against holds the letter

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Grandad, objecting to the instructions, makes a quick bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Popcorn is popped maize kernels, an airy snack eaten in small handfuls.

clue.text: Belgian city lord

definitions.meaning: a city in eastern Belgium on the Meuse
a feudal superior to whom allegiance is owed

explanation.definitionFit: Liège is a major Belgian city, and a liege is a feudal lord owed loyalty by vassals.

clue.text: Host's pretty good shot besieging stronghold

indicators.note: besieging means surrounding, so the shot wraps round the fortress

parts.note: in archery or shooting, an inner is a hit in the ring just outside the bull
a keep is the strongest tower of a castle

explanation.surface: A host's marksman scoring well while laying siege to a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host's' is Host is, with 'is' as the link. An inner is a shot just off the bullseye.
explanation.definitionFit: An innkeeper runs an inn and acts as host to guests.

clue.text: Tellurium's not radioactive as can be proved experimentally

parts.note: Te is the chemical symbol for tellurium
a stable isotope does not decay radioactively

explanation.surface: Tellurium is not radioactive, as experiments can demonstrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something testable can be checked or verified by experiment.

clue.text: Past history revolutionary holds that's surprising!

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the word for revolutionary goes round the exclamation

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist revolutionary
cor is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's past background contains something astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: Cor is everyday British slang for 'Wow!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A record is an account of past events, such as a criminal or employment history.
